chunks: And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Whoever recites 'Say, O you disbelievers' and 'Say, He is Allah, [the] One' in one of the obligatory prayers, Allah grants forgiveness for him, for his parents, and for his children. And if he was unfortunate, his name is erased from the register of the unfortunate and established in the register of the happy. And Allah keeps him alive as happy, causes him to die as a martyr, and raises him as a martyr.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Kafirun and Surah Al-Ikhlas in obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the transformative power of these two Surahs, which are often recited together in Fajr prayer, as a means of elevating one's spiritual status from the 'register of the wretched' to that of the 'blessed.' This narration underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory merit of Quranic recitation, extending divine forgiveness not only to the individual but also to their parents and offspring, effectively altering their eschatological destiny.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam as-Sadiq (a.s.) said: Whoever recites Surah Kafiroon and Surah Tauheed in one of his obligatory prayers, Allah grants  forgiveness  for  him,  for  his  parents  and  for  his children,  and  if  his  name  is  written  in  the  register  of unfortunate and disobedient persons, then after erasing it He writes   in it the register of virtuous and happy people and Allah would grant him the death of a martyr and raise him on the Day of Judgment with the martyrs.
